subject: hoverPickup
pitch:
Category: Vehicle.
Subject: militarized pickup converted to hover thrusters.
Style: low-poly cyberpunk.
reasoning:
I'm planning a compact but detailed module for a militarized hover-converted pickup truck—replacing wheels with ducted-fan thrusters at each corner, adding armored skirt panels, a roof turret with minigun or railgun, a bed-mounted missile pod, and neon underglow with a light bar for visual flair.

I'm working out the physical layout: setting a hover height so the lowest surfaces sit just above the floor, deciding on a chassis joint plus fan-spin joints and turret yaw/pitch joints for articulation, and sketching coordinates for the body and four thruster nacelles at the truck's corners using simple cylinder and torus shapes to form open-ended ducts.

Now I'm shaping the duct silhouette with a closed lathe profile, adding a spinning fan and a downward-facing glow disc inside each nacelle, and connecting struts from the nacelles to the chassis. For the body material I'm pulling in a clockwork kit for panelled metal paint in a cyberpunk gunmetal palette accented with neon magenta and cyan, and planning SVG decals for hazard stripes, a unit-number neon sign, a skull emblem, warning labels, and a screen texture.

I'm defining helper functions for boxes, cylinders, part placement, and decal planes, then laying out the chassis joint and floor pan dimensions before positioning the hover nacelles outboard on either side of the body so they clear its width.

Now I'm adjusting nacelle positions and connecting pylons, then blocking out the cab, hood, and bed sections with their respective box and sloped frustum dimensions.

Adding greenhouse glass, roof, and pillars...

Planning the remaining pieces now: a roof turret with a glowing cannon tip, rear missile pods with a neon sign, antenna and light bar, magenta underglow strips, and cyan thruster glow. I'm also sketching the front plough with spikes, slit headlights, camera mirrors, and twin tailpipe thrusters at the rear, while settling on panelled iron and mottled olive-drab materials for the hull and armor plating before writing the actual construction code.

Defining nacelle geometry...

Still working out fan blade geometry...

Checking the hover height so the glow ring stays near the floor, then adding underglow strips along the body edges for extra lighting. I'm also considering a hazard-stripe texture on the bumper face, thinking through how to render diagonal yellow/black stripes as a plane pattern.

Then there's a skull emblem decal for the doors, placed on side-facing planes so it reads correctly from either side, and a unit number text decal for the roof, worked out so the orientation looks right when viewed from behind.

For the tailgate I want a glowing neon sign texture, but going with latin text like "NOVA//9" instead of kanji to avoid font fallback issues, applying a glow effect to that plane. I'm also adding a small radar panel texture glowing on the back of the cab, giving five total decal textures: hazard stripes, skull, unit text, neon sign, and radar.

For the interior, I'm keeping it simple with seat boxes and a glowing dashboard. Now I'm working out where to place the turret's yaw joint on the roof.

I'm detailing the turret structure—a yaw joint rotating around the vertical axis and a pitch joint aiming forward, with parts including a ring torus base, drum, cheek plates, trunnion rod, twin barrels extending forward, a muzzle brake, glowing cyan coil rings along the barrels for a railgun look, plus an ammo box and sensor.

For the truck bed, I'm adding a missile pod launcher on a pedestal with six tubes and spiked missile noses, spare fuel cell cylinders, and twin rear thruster bells with glowing discs at the tail. I'm also planning cab details like door seams, handles, slanted armor plates, mirror camera pods, and wedge-shaped hover fenders.

Now I'm sketching the hood as a tapered frustum box sloping slightly from front to back, roof light bar with alternating magenta/cyan glow strips, antenna whips using spike helpers, and setting up a reusable part-creation wrapper bound to the chassis bone with mirrored loops for left/right symmetry.

For glass I'll use a dark cyan flat color, checking that gun parts attach to the pitch bone and the overall vehicle height and ground clearance look right before finalizing the paint palette and writing out the full build code with bolt rows, panel seams, hood exhaust vents, and side skirt armor between the nacelles.

I'm sketching out the skull decal SVG with glowing eye polygons and teeth, then the hazard stripe SVG with alternating yellow and black parallelograms, before placing door decals on the cab sides with the right position and plane orientation.
